title: Functional Analysis I
purpose: Normed and Banach spaces, bounded operators and the four big theorems; Lebesgue measure and integration; Hilbert space and the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators, studied with complete proofs from the MIT 18.102 (Spring 2021) lecture notes and original Corniversity exercises.
description:
Functional analysis is linear algebra and analysis done in spaces of functions, where the familiar finite-dimensional comforts (all norms equivalent, closed bounded sets compact, every linear map continuous) fail. This course builds the replacements: completeness, the operator norm, Baire category and its consequences (uniform boundedness, open mapping, closed graph), Hahn–Banach, then enough Lebesgue theory to make $L^p$ spaces honest Banach spaces, then Hilbert space, orthonormal bases, the Riesz representation theorem, adjoints, compact operators and the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators, ending with the Dirichlet problem on an interval.

**How this adaptation works.** The spine is the complete set of 23 per-lecture notes from MIT OpenCourseWare 18.102 Introduction to Functional Analysis, Spring 2021 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), with lecturer Casey Rodriguez and notes by Andrew Lin. Corniversity re-paces the 23 lectures as 12 units for a term of ten teaching weeks plus a reading week and a synthesis week, keeps the notes' numbering of definitions and theorems so citations are exact, and sets its own exercises with hint ladders and rubrics. Where an exercise is adapted from the source it says so.

**Prepared course.** All twelve units contain lecture notes, exact readings, original problems with progressive hints, instructor-only reference reasoning and cumulative synthesis. Some deep theorems have explicitly named source-proof dependencies or an identified proof-sketch boundary; these are stated in the relevant lessons. No course generation or subscription call is needed to study this authored material. Structural readiness does not imply external academic certification; review evidence and remaining limits are recorded separately.

outcomes.description: State the definitions of normed, Banach and Hilbert spaces and decide, with proof, whether a given space is complete.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Proof attempts on completeness exercises, including a counterexample for an incomplete normed space.

outcomes.description: Work with bounded linear operators: prove boundedness, compute or bound operator norms, and use the completeness of B(V,W).
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Operator-norm calculations with justification and at least one unboundedness argument.

outcomes.description: Apply the Baire category, uniform boundedness, open mapping and closed graph theorems with their hypotheses explicit.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Proofs that name the completeness hypothesis used and a counterexample when it is dropped.

outcomes.description: Use the Hahn–Banach theorem to extend functionals and to separate points, and explain the double dual.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Unit05 exercise4: complete real/complex Hahn–Banach proof with norm preservation and bidual isometry; the other unit05 tasks assess separation and reflexivity applications.

outcomes.description: Construct Lebesgue measure and the Lebesgue integral and apply the convergence theorems to prove completeness of L^p.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Measure/integral and convergence sheets in units06–08, plus unit08 exercise4: complete Lp completeness proof for 1≤p≤∞, with a separate essential-uniform endpoint argument.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators, including to a boundary-value problem on an interval.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Unit12 exercise4: complete compact self-adjoint spectral-theorem proof including the kernel and zero-spectrum cases; unit12 exercises1–3: Green approximation, resonance and variable-potential Dirichlet applications.

assessmentSpecs.title: Problem sets
assessmentSpecs.description: Each unit's exercises are submitted as immutable attempts and assessed with line-localised feedback. Revision is expected; the portfolio is the record of attempts and revisions, not a single mark.

assessmentSpecs.title: Mid-course synthesis
assessmentSpecs.description: Complete MAT-230-u06-ex4 after unit06: a concrete mid-course proof portfolio connecting quotient completeness, the Baire/open-mapping and uniform-boundedness arguments, Hahn–Banach separation, and category versus measure. The linked unit activity supplies the prompt, progressive hints, full instructor solution and criterion weights. Open book and untimed by default; estimated 170 minutes for a first written attempt.

assessmentSpecs.title: Final synthesis: the Dirichlet problem
assessmentSpecs.description: Complete MAT-230-u12-ex4 as the proof component: derive the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem from the allowed Hilbert-space facts, including extremal eigenvectors, completeness, kernel and spectrum. Complete unit12 exercises1–3 as the application component: truncation errors, resonance and the variable-potential Dirichlet problem with regularity justified. Optional oral explanation supplements, rather than replaces, the written evidence.
rubricSummary: correct use of the spectral theorem

externalSyllabusNote: Adapted study path using MIT OpenCourseWare 18.102 (Spring 2021) materials under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The original course ran 23 lectures with weekly homework, a 24-hour take-home midterm and a 48-hour final assignment. Corniversity re-paces it as 12 units, keeps the notes' statement numbering, and sets its own exercises and assessments. This is not an MIT course and confers no credit anywhere.
